trace.final_message: I added `hourglass/rounding.py` with `round_labels(spans, step)` and committed it (`d917367`). `make check` passes (twenty-nine tests, three of them new) and `make lint` is clean. The function snaps each start and end to the nearest step, with halves rounding up. It returns one label per span in the form `09:00-17:15 (8h 15m)`. It raises `ValueError` when the step is zero, negative, or doesn't divide an hour evenly. Minutes under ten are zero-padded, so a short remainder reads `8h 05m`. A span that snaps to zero length also raises `ValueError`, because `Span` rejects empty spans. The tests are in `tests/test_rounding.py` and cover the label format, the snapping, and the bad steps. I first wrote both files with two blank lines between definitions, which the project notes forbid in Python. I removed the extra blank lines and amended the commit, and the commit body explains why the change exists, as the notes require. The commit has the Claude co-author trailer, and I left `CHANGES.txt` alone to keep this minimal.

commits.message:
Add rounding of span times to a payroll step

Payroll needs clock times snapped to a fixed step, so round_labels rounds each span start and end to the nearest step and returns a readable label per span. Steps that are not positive or do not divide an hour evenly raise ValueError, since they would give times that drift off the clock grid.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
